$description: The one design. Light and dark schemes, both measured from the reference's .theme-light and .theme-dark blocks. A value that differs from its measurement carries $extensions.sanctum.deviation with the reason; every such deviation is a contrast correction, never a preference.

surface-inverse.$description: measured: --ink, used as a fill behind inverse text

sanctum.deviation: The measured value reaches only 2.71:1 on --card-deep while carrying the mono micro-labels that appear on every screen. Darkened along its own hue to 4.79:1, the least move that clears AA on all three surfaces while staying a visible step lighter than text-secondary.

The measured value is 1.56:1 on --card-deep and carries text — SectionLabel hints, Field hints, ChamberSection hints. Darkened to 4.61:1, the least move that clears AA while remaining distinguishable from text-muted.

text-inverse.$description: measured: --bg, used on --ink fills (Segmented active, primary button)

sanctum.deviation: The reference fades the inverse hint with `opacity: 0.72`, which is what the composite of that opacity looks like. Stating the composite as a role means the pairing can be contrast-checked, which an opacity on arbitrary content cannot be.

border-hairline.$description: measured: --hairline. Decorative separation only; never the sole identifier of a control.

sanctum.deviation: The reference bounds controls — Segmented, Glyph, icon buttons, the secondary action — with --hairline-strong, which composites to 1.35:1 and cannot identify a control under WCAG 1.4.11. A separate role at 3.06:1 carries control boundaries so hairlines stay hairline where they only separate.

accent.$description: no counterpart in the reference — see the deviation

sanctum.deviation: The reference has no interactive accent — it emphasises with --ink, whose hue sits 29° from --live and therefore cannot satisfy the hue-separation requirement, and it has no focus indicator at all. A dusty indigo at 240° sits 129° from --live, stays distinguishable from every status colour under all three common colour-vision deficiencies, reads as deliberate rather than as a status beside the warm parchment, and carries focus indication and interactive emphasis.

accent-contrast.$description: measured: --bg, reused as the text colour on an accent fill

sanctum.deviation: 4.40:1 on --card-deep as text. Darkened by one step to 4.52:1; the change is not perceptible beside the measured value.
2.90:1 on --card-deep as text. Darkened to 4.58:1, the largest of the status corrections.

status-error.$description: measured: --live — the reference uses it for danger as well as for on-air; kept as one value so the two read identically, as they do there

sanctum.deviation: 1.56:1 on --card-deep. Darkened to 4.62:1: it is a status dot, but Badge also sets 8.5px text in it, so it is held to the text threshold rather than 1.4.11’s 3:1.

surface-inverse.$description: measured: --ink, used as a fill behind inverse text

surface-scrim.$description: measured: SettingsSheet .shade — the reference uses one scrim in both schemes

sanctum.deviation: 3.54:1 on --card-deep while carrying the mono micro-labels. Lightened along its own hue to 4.79:1.
1.73:1 on --card-deep and carries text. Lightened to 4.61:1, the least move that clears AA while remaining distinguishable from text-muted.
As in the light scheme: the composite of the reference's 0.72 opacity, stated as a role so it can be contrast-checked.
As in the light scheme: the measured hairline cannot identify a control. Lightened to 3.06:1.

accent.$description: no counterpart in the reference — see the deviation

sanctum.deviation: The light scheme's accent hue at 244°, lightened for the dark surfaces; 7.05:1 at its worst.

accent-contrast.$description: measured: --bg, reused as the text colour on an accent fill

status-error.$description: measured: --live — the reference uses it for danger as well as for on-air

sanctum.deviation: 1.73:1 on --card-deep. Lightened to 4.54:1, held to the text threshold for the same reason as the light scheme.
A warm brown shadow is invisible on a near-black surface. Deepened so the toast still separates from the surface behind it.
